subject: Operator certification, test-access plan, and MSA exhibit questions
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stellarhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com, Samir Rao <samir.rao@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy - operator certification & test access request

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Quick one from our side as we prepare the order form and exhibits for the private deployment: the security team has asked for formal evidence that any on-site/operator-level access will be both certified and testable prior to go-live. Specifically they want:

- A short operator certification checklist (who has access, training record, background checks).
- A timeboxed test-access window plan so Stellar Security can validate a read-only snapshot and confirm separation boundaries.
- Confirmation of the proposed Exhibit in the MSA that covers operator responsibilities and any escrow/third-party snapshot process.

Can you share an initial checklist and a proposed test schedule this week? Also, if you have a redline for Exhibit B (operator access & snapshot protocol), please attach — our legal wants to start reviewing before procurement finalizes the order form.

We may also need a contact for a technical runbook owner we can test against (Samir CC'd).

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Procurement
Stellar Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@stellarhealth.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy - operator certification & test access request

Thanks Ellen — appreciate the clear ask.

Summary of what we can provide this week: 
- Operator certification checklist (draft attached). It includes roles, minimum background checks we run, and training artifacts we can share under NDA. [attachment: operator_cert_checklist_v1.pdf]
- Snapshot validation plan (spreadsheet attached) that lays out: snapshot cadence, how we generate a read-only snapshot, scrub rules for PHI/PII, and the access window steps for Stellar Security to run validation. [attachment: snapshot-validation-plan.xlsx]
- A proposed redline for Exhibit B to the MSA focused on operator responsibilities and permitted on-prem actions. This is an initial internal draft; legal will need to sign off before we circulate externally. [attachment: MSA_Exhibit_B_redlines_20261120.docx]

Proposed short schedule:
- Tue 2026-11-23: internal review at Redwood (legal + ops)
- Thu 2026-11-25: deliverables to Stellar (checklist + plan + redline)
- Tue 2026-12-01: 2-hour validation window (tentative) for Stellar Security to exercise read-only snapshot and confirm boundaries

Runbook owner: Connor O'Brien (ops lead) — connor.obrien@redwood.com. He'll be the technical point for the validation window.

Notes on evidence scope (callouts for legal):
- Our snapshot process removes direct identifiers by default; we can provide a deterministic scrub report describing methods but cannot provide raw PHI/PII.
- For escrow-like requests (operator snapshot handover), we typically propose a witnessed transfer model rather than long-term custody — happy to outline options.

Laura — flagging for legal redlines. Connor, can you confirm the validation window steps and whether we need a staging token or temporary console access?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@stellarhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stellarhealth.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy - operator certification & test access request

Thanks Marcus — that looks like a good start. A few clarifying points from Security: 

- Validation window: we prefer a maximum 2-hour window where Stellar runs a pre-defined checklist against a read-only snapshot. We do not need console-level SSH access; a signed URL with time-bound read-only access to the snapshot artifacts is sufficient.
- Scrub proofs: the scrub report should include the exact transform steps and a CRC/hash of the post-scrub sample so we can verify the same artifact across transfers.
- Witnessed transfer vs custody: Stellar strongly prefers a witnessed transfer (Redwood provides snapshot + hash, an independent auditor validates) rather than long-term custody. If custody is requested in the contract, we will need indemnities and SLA carveouts.

Can Connor propose exact endpoints/URLs and token TTL for the validation run? We can tentatively reserve Tue 12/01 09:00–11:00 PT for the window; please confirm.

Samir
Samir Rao
Sr. Security Engineer
Stellar Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stellarhealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@stellarhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy - operator certification & test access request

Ellen / Samir — thanks for the quick turn. A few legal clarifications and next steps so procurement has a clean path forward: 

1) Exhibit redline: we've reviewed the initial Exhibit B redline (attached) and made two substantive changes to reflect the witnessed-transfer preference: 
   - Section 2(a): replace "custody handover" language with "witnessed transfer with hash verification"
   - Section 4: add indemnity carveout if Stellar requires long-term custody of a snapshot

2) Attestations & evidence: Redwood will provide the operator certification checklist and a limited set of training records under an evidence-sharing NDA. We will not provide background-check PII; instead we'll include date-stamped attestations signed by HR and ops leads.

3) Validation mechanics: Connor confirmed we can provide a signed, time-limited URL to an S3 bucket containing the scrubbed snapshot artifacts. Token TTL = 2 hours. We will also generate a SHA256 hash for each artifact and a short scrub methodology appendix. Connor (ops) and I (legal) will be on the call during the validation window.

4) Procurement items: Ellen — if you can confirm the PO target date, we'll prepare a final Exhibit B and an order-form exhibit that maps the validation window and responsibilities.

Attachments included: final_redline_ExhibitB_20261201.docx, operator_cert_checklist_v1.pdf, snapshot-validation-plan.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
